findings.title: No wire-body test that user_context reaches the MCP-Connect payload
findings.problem: The EPMCDME-13260 deliverable is that user_context (with extra_attributes stripped) is serialised into the JSON body POSTed to MCP-Connect on tools/call and tools/list. The new tests only assert MCPExecutionContext.to_request_fields() dict output (test_models.py) and masked DEBUG-log text (test_client.py TestMCPConnectClientUserContextDebugLog); none inspect post.call_args / the post_body built by _build_request_payload. MCPToolInvocationRequest.user_context (models.py:510) sits next to five sibling fields that all carry Field(exclude=True).
findings.impact: A regression that adds Field(exclude=True) to MCPToolInvocationRequest.user_context, or re-adds user_context to an exclude set at client.py:128, would stop the profile reaching MCP-Connect and silently turn EPMCDME-13260 into a no-op with the full test suite still green. The DSP path guards against the equivalent regression (test_provider_tool_factory.py asserts invocation_request.user_context); the MCP path has no such assertion.
findings.recommendation: In tests/codemie/service/mcp/test_client.py, after invoke_tool(...) and list_tools(...) with an MCPExecutionContext whose user_context is set, assert post.call_args.kwargs['json']['user_context'] equals the expected non-sensitive profile dict and that 'extra_attributes' is not in it.
